# Japanese loanwords from Portuguese (katakana forms)
# Source: https://www.sljfaq.org/afaq/portuguese.html
#   "Which Japanese words come from Portuguese?" - sci.lang.japan FAQ (Ben Bullock)
# Fetched: 2026-09-21 (single web_fetch, page returned in full, not truncated)
# Entries: 33
# Format: portuguese_word:katakana  (keys lowercased, ASCII-folded, punctuation stripped)
# Katakana is copied verbatim from the FAQ entry brackets; only the katakana spelling
#   is kept (kanji/▽-marked variants and hiragana-only spellings are omitted).
# Page entries not included here because the FAQ lists no katakana-only form:
#   joro (jorro, 如雨露/じょうろ), kanakin (canequim, かなきん), tempura (temporas, てんぷら),
#   pin kara kiri made (pinta/cruz, ピンからキリまで contains hiragana).
# sabao maps to two FAQ entries (saboten サボテン "may have come from", shabon シャボン
#   "came from"); the directly attested one, shabon, is kept for the duplicate key.
